# The optimizer splices a component whose body it can fold into its caller
# before lowering, and the body's emits are the call site's handlers there as
# in the lowering's inliners. They were left standing: a handler the call site
# wrote never ran -- `emit("chose", x)` in a test build of `app`, against
# nothing the Go targets define -- and an event it did not handle became one
# of the caller's own (`emit("change", k)` from sngl:ui's tabs).

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component pick(items list[string], @chose(s string)) ui.node {
    for var x = items {
        ui.button #opt(text=x, @click {
            chose(x)
        })
    }
}

component app ui.node {
    var last = ""
    pick #p(items=["a", "b"], @chose(s) {
        last = s
    })
}

func testTheCallSitesHandlerRuns(t Test, c app) {
    c.p.opt[1].click()
    t.assert(c.last == "b")
}

// A library body's emit the call site handles no event for is nothing: in a
// build rooted at `app` it used to be left as an emit of `app`'s own, which
// declares none.
component plain ui.node {
    var idx = 0
    ui.tabs(:selected=idx) {
        ui.tab(label="one")
    }
}

func testAnUnhandledEventIsNothing(t Test, c plain) {
    t.assert(c.idx == 0)
}

ui.window {
    app
    plain
}
